recurring_harms: discriminatory opportunity loss;reduced recruiter attention;inaccessible application journey;privacy loss;opaque vendor accountability
human_in_loop_decisions: An authorized recruiter with sufficient time, original application evidence, uncertainty information, and override authority must review every complete application and decide shortlist, hold, rejection, or reinstatement; an independent reviewer must decide appeals without hiring-manager or vendor conflict.
strongest_guardrails: Narrow job-related intended use; deterministic complete-queue exposure; independent validity and subgroup evaluation; protected-attribute separation; accessible accommodation and manual alternative; model status-write prohibition; versioned logs; usable manual fallback; appeal, pause, re-review, and independent restart gates
cross_industry_pattern: Across the three HR-recruitment cases, harm did not arise from model accuracy alone: explicit discriminatory rules, historical labels and proxies, vendor integration, inaccessible journeys, and weak oversight could restrict access to employment. The product roadmap must therefore close human-review, fairness-validity, accessibility, privacy, monitoring, and legal-classification gates before recommendations influence live hiring.
